Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below and I can follow up with a one-page pricing table + SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

1) Separate pools vs. global commit: we can do either. Separate region pools are priced per-region (reflecting local capacity costs) and are simpler from a capacity isolation/compliance standpoint. Global/pooled commits offer better utilization and therefore higher effective discounts but require cross-region routing controls.

2) Throughput guarantees: for an 8x A100-equivalent pool we guarantee baseline throughput of ~120K tokens/min for short-sequence inference (<= 512 tokens) with a 99th percentile latency SLO of 220ms for single-stream requests. For batched workloads throughput scales linearly with sustained batch sizing; we’ll include a throughput matrix in the PDF.

3) Failover billing: by default, failover is DR-ready but billed only for active capacity. If you want hot-standby (replicated pools in EU-West reserved and kept warm), that is billed as reserved capacity in both regions. We offer a lower-priced warm-standby option (reduced commit, faster spin-up) — details in the attachment I’ll send.

4) Commit discounts: 24–36 month commits get stepped discounts (tiered by total vGPU-hours). We can model a blended discount if you commit to identical pool sizes in both regions. Also flexible payment terms (annual vs. monthly invoicing) are negotiable at enterprise scale.

I'll attach a draft pricing table and SOW. Would you prefer separate line items per region or a blended quote that shows both options?

Best,
Jordan Blake

Priya — attaching the proposal + draft SOW per your ask. Key points summarized here so procurement has a one-pager to attach:

Attachment: Dedicated_MultiRegion_Proposal_v1.pdf (pricing table)
Attachment: SOW_AvaCloud_Redwood_draft.docx (ops/SLA draft)

Summary highlights:
- Option A (Separate pools):
  • US-East: 8x A100-equivalent reserved pool — baseline throughput guarantee: 120K tokens/min; 99th pctl latency SLO: 220ms.
  • EU-West: 8x A100-equivalent reserved pool — identical baseline SLOs; region multiplier +8% on unit price.
  • Billing: reserved commitments billed monthly; warm-standby is a configurable option billed at 30% of full reserved rate when flagged as "standby". Standby spin-up guaranteed <= 10 minutes.

- Option B (Blended/global commit):
  • Single committed quantity (16x effective vGPU capacity) with cross-region routing. Effective blended rate offers an incremental 12% discount vs. separate pools due to utilization efficiencies.

- Failover behavior and billing:
  • Cold-standby (no reserved capacity in DR): no additional region billing until failover occurs (metered on-demand rates apply during failover).
  • Warm-standby: billed at 30% committed rate and supports KV cache priming; RTO <= 10m, RPO <= 30s for cache metadata replication (payload replication depends on your storage choices).

- Example blended effective rate (36-month term, annual invoicing):
  • 2 x 8-GPU reserved pools (US + EU) — blended effective rate: $2.45 / vGPU-hour (after tiered discounts).
  • Separate region line items shown in the attached PDF for your finance team.

Next steps: 1) confirm which option (A or B) procurement prefers; 2) we finalize SOW and DocuSign packet for signature; 3) engineering kickoff for region-specific routing rules.

Jordan
